findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:81 declares five registered discovery adapters, but buildResult assigns the same preassembled input.pathRefs to process_fact_registry, handler_dispatch_inventory, and static_call_graph, while runtime_trace performs no discovery. runAcceptanceDiscoveryAdapters only relabels this one input set; it never inspects handler/dispatch source, a static graph, or runtime facts. Because deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis constructs input.pathRefs from the topology/planned declarations themselves, the adapters cannot independently discover an omitted path or naturally disagree and can falsely classify the self-described closure complete. This violates Wave 1A's independent registered-adapter exit condition.

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:160 computes closureFilesHash from only planned endpoint files; registered producer/consumer closure entries are appended as literal inventory strings and their referenced source files are never resolved or content-hashed. deriveRegisteredProcessFactClosure likewise emits producer/consumer labels rather than resolvable source paths (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:44). Therefore an out-of-scope registered consumer can change while closureFilesHash remains unchanged, defeating the receipt freshness binding explicitly required by Wave 1A.

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:278 contains the only topology-versus-basis and exclusion validation, but neither deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis nor the production generate/read handlers call it (handlers/proofstory.ts:134-184,206-234). Worse, derivation seeds every topology path into expectedPathRefs at lines 194-203 and the echo adapters reproduce it, so an invented topology path can be absorbed into a complete signed basis. The smoke calls reconcileTopologyWithCoverageBasis directly, which does not prove the real acceptance_basis_generate/acceptance_basis path rejects the mutation.
